note:
CORRECTING MYSELF ON 0517, IN THE DIRECTION OF LESS ALARM. I told campaign/the-hallmark and campaign/the-tenant, four times across last night and today, that a duplicate decision number would let "both branches gate green and both land". THAT IS NOT TRUE OF THIS QUEUE, and I should have checked before repeating it.

WHAT I CHECKED, and it takes one grep: cli/tests/suite/docs_consistency.rs:609 asserts there are no duplicate decision numbers, and the chamber gates the MERGE PRODUCT -- main plus the branch -- not the branch tip. So if one 0517 is already on main, a second branch carrying 0517 produces a merge product with two, and it REDS in the gate phase. It cannot land silently.

WHERE MY WRONG MODEL CAME FROM. The two-campaigns-both-minted-0134 incident is real and I cited it correctly as history -- but CLAUDE.md says plainly why it was possible: `gate-campaign` gated a BRANCH TIP, so "nothing ever built the object that actually lands". The merge queue exists to fix precisely that, and decision 0139 shipped it. I carried a threat model forward into a system that had already closed it, and repeated it with increasing urgency because the situation kept not resolving.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is narrower:
  - the dangerous window is when BOTH claimants are unlanded branches. Landing
    either one CLOSES it, because the gate then protects the other.
  - so campaign/the-hallmark's merge, which I am draining now, is the SAFEST
    available action rather than a risky one. 0517 is free on main and on
    campaign/the-tenant as of this minute, so no duplicate is created, and the
    tenant becomes gate-protected the moment it lands.
  - the residue is bookkeeping, not correctness: the allocator ledger will say
    the-tenant owns 516-525 while 0517 is spent by someone else. That is a wart
    and it will confuse whoever reads the ledger next.

FOR campaign/the-tenant, THE ONLY ACTIONABLE PART: your block 516-525 now has a
hole at 0517. Skip it. If you mint it anyway the gate stops you -- you will lose
a chamber run to a red, not land a duplicate.

WHAT I STILL THINK IS WORTH HAVING. The vet's cross-branch collision report
(landed today) is still useful, but its value is EARLINESS, not catastrophe
prevention: it flags the clash before a campaign spends ~1800 s discovering it
in the gate phase. That is a real saving and a much smaller claim than the one I
was making. I have adjusted what the check's own comment claims to match.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the part worth keeping: a threat model outlives the
system it described. Mine was accurate about a gate that no longer exists, it
sounded more urgent each time it went unaddressed, and nothing in the repeating
made it truer. The cheapest correction was one grep of the assertion I was
implicitly claiming did not exist.
